facts.Course: Air Traffic Management / Air Navigation Services

blocks.text: An Aeronautical Information Specialist (AIS Specialist) manages, verifies, processes, and distributes information that pilots, air traffic controllers, flight-planning teams, and other aviation professionals need to conduct safe and efficient flights.
The role supports the aviation information system by ensuring that aeronautical data is accurate, consistent, current, traceable, and available to authorized users.
The work may involve aeronautical charts, airport information, airspace structures, navigation aids, runways, flight procedures, temporary restrictions, and official aviation publications.

items.text: Collect and validate aeronautical data from authorized sources.
Process changes to airports, runways, airspace, and navigation facilities.
Maintain aeronautical information publications and related datasets.
Support Notices to Airmen (NOTAM) processing and distribution, according to assigned responsibilities.
Check data quality, consistency, and completeness.
Coordinate with airports, air traffic services, aviation authorities, and data originators.
Follow publication schedules and change-management procedures.
Maintain audit trails and controlled records.
Support digital aeronautical information management systems.
Help ensure that pilots and operational teams receive reliable information.

blocks.label: Important distinction
blocks.text: AIS focuses on aeronautical information management and publication. Air traffic controllers manage aircraft movements operationally. An AIS Specialist does not automatically qualify as an air traffic controller; separate training, licensing, and eligibility requirements may apply.
AIM means Aeronautical Information Management. It represents the broader transition from traditional publication-focused AIS processes toward data-centric digital information management.
Build the foundation in aviation operations, geography, mathematics, and information management.

items.text: Research airport facilities and operational information.

blocks.label: Year-1 target
blocks.text: Understand the basic aviation environment and how accurate information supports flight safety.
Study the core processes involved in collecting, validating, maintaining, and publishing aeronautical information.
The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) establishes international provisions for aeronautical information services through Annex 15 and related procedures in PANS-AIM.
